briefdescription.para: Can load/store 2 registers/cycle.
Can load/store 2 registers/cycle, but needs an extra cycle if the access is not 64-bit aligned.
Can load/store 1 register/cycle.
Can load/store 1 register/cycle, but needs an extra cycle for address computation and potentially also for register writeback.
What kind of timing do load multiple/store multiple instructions have.
All GPRs can be pushed in a single instruction.
R7 and LR must be adjacent, because R7 is the frame pointer, and must point to a frame record consisting of the previous frame pointer and the return address.

detaileddescription.para: push {r0-r7, lr} push {r8-r12} vpush {d8-d15} Note that Thumb1 changes this layout when the frame pointer is R11, using a longer sequence of instructions because R11 can't be used by a Thumb1 push instruction. This doesn't currently have a separate enum value, and is handled entriely within Thumb1FrameLowering::emitPrologue.

briefdescription.para: When the stack frame size is not known (because of variable-sized objects or realignment), Windows SEH requires the callee-saved registers to be stored in three regions, with R11 and LR below the floating-point registers.
When generating AAPCS-compilant frame chains, R11 is the frame pointer, and must be pushed adjacent to the return address (LR).

detaileddescription.para: Normally this isn't a problem, because the only register between them is r12, which is the intra-procedure-call scratch register, so doesn't need to be saved. However, when PACBTI is in use, r12 contains the authentication code, so does need to be saved. This means that we need a separate push for R11 and LR. push {r0-r10, r12} push {r11, lr} vpush {d8-d15}

briefdescription.para: How the push and pop instructions of callee saved general-purpose registers should be split.
